verdict.rationale: Skyvern publishes a dedicated versioning-and-deprecation page. It promises at least 6 months notice before an endpoint is sunset and at least 12 months before a major version is removed. It also commits to RFC 9745/8594 Deprecation/Sunset headers and to marking `deprecated: true` in the OpenAPI spec, and the API itself is versioned under /v1/ paths. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the policy is honored in practice, and evidence of a changelog showing past deprecations.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy

citations.quote: At least 6 months notice. That is the minimum time between the deprecation announcement and the sunset date on which the endpoint stops serving traffic. Removing an entire major version gets at least 12 months
Machine-readable response headers on every response from a deprecated endpoint, following RFC 9745 (Deprecation) and RFC 8594 (Sunset)
with run endpoints such as POST /v1/run/tasks
